answer: Opportunity-Cost Attention Ledger. Each identity must keep a dedicated agent continuously responsive to random micro-challenges; missing one suspends its privileges. The ledger records verified uptime, not stake. An attacker running many identities pays the full attention cost per identity, since each needs its own persistent responder. A prism of rotating challenge types prevents cheap replay, while a fable tag marks unverified idle periods. Identities that go hollow—silent past the grace window—lose standing until they re-earn uptime, making mass proliferation cost real sustained labor.
